away.headline: 3 Colts out vs. Vikings with injuries; 4 questionable
away.blurb: Ahead of Sunday's Week 7 game against the Minnesota Vikings , the Indianapolis Colts have ruled three players out and four others questionable. CB Sauce Gardner (calf), TE Tyler Warren (groin), and WR Anthony Gould (concussion) are all out. For more on the impact of those absences, you can find that here . Questionable for this matchup are LB CJ Allen (ankle), LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), P Rigoberto Sanchez (foot), and CB Justin Walley (knee). Allen appeared on the injury report on Thursday and then did not practice on Friday. Boettcher was a non-participant on Friday as well. Potentially without these two, the Colts ' linebacker depth would be hampered. As a result, we could see Germaine Pratt elevated from the practice squad. Walley was limited the final two days after not practicing on Wednesday. If he can't go, we could see Kapena Gushiken in the slot, with Cam Taylor-Britt likely starting outside in Gardner's absence. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: 3 Colts out vs. Vikings with injuries; 4 questionable With Jaylon Carlies back, the Colts will have their starters at linebacker between him and Akeem Davis-Gaither. Sanchez's injury occurred in Sunday's loss on the blocked punt. As insurance at this position, the Colts signed veteran Thomas Morstead to the practice squad.

away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. home.headline: Murray Set To Play: QB expected to start vs Colts; Vikings urged to attack downfield
home.source: The Times of India on MSN
home.blurb: Running back Jordan Mason presents a different situation. He is preparing to return from injured reserve but remains questionable with a thumb injury. His status could affect Minnesota's plans in the running game and influence how the Vikings distribute their offensive workload. Note: This update reflects the supplied report dated October 24, 2026. Confirm the official inactive list before kickoff, as the available information does not independently verify Murray's final game status. Kyler Murray faces a key test as the Minnesota Vikings prepare to take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. The quarterback could have a valuable opportunity to exploit a struggling pass rush, but Minnesota must make the right decisions to turn that advantage into points. The latest injury report offers encouraging news for the Vikings' receiving group, giving Murray potential options at every level of the field. However, the bigger question is whether Minnesota can move away from its reliance on short screen passes and make the most of the time its quarterback may have in the pocket. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Will Kyler Murray play against the Indianapolis Colts today? Minnesota also received positive news about its key offensive weapons. Wide receiver Justin Jefferson, tight end T.J. Hockenson and wide receiver Jordan Addison all practised in full and carry no game designation, according to the report. Their availability could give Murray more options as he looks to challenge Indianapolis through the air. Kyler Murray's injury update and matchup against the Colts That weakness could give Murray more time to read the field and allow receivers to find space downfield. Jefferson and Addison offer options for deeper throws, while Hockenson can provide a target over the middle. However, Indianapolis can still make life difficult for the Vikings. The Colts often use eight defenders in coverage, limiting open passing lanes and encouraging quarterbacks to throw underneath. Minnesota must recognise when a short pass makes sense and when a more aggressive option offers greater value. The Vikings' heavy use of screen passes has become a concern because the approach has not consistently produced efficient results. Against a defence that struggles to generate pressure, Murray and head coach Kevin O'Connell have a chance to change that pattern. The key will be balance. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals MIAMI DOLPHINS Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win Joe Schad Palm Beach Post Updated Oct. 23, 2026, 12:24 p.m. ET The winless Miami Dolphins are looking to reset after a bye week and secure their first victory against the New York Jets. Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. away.headline: Is Breece Hall Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Dolphins vs. Jets in NFL Week 7)
away.blurb: New York Jets running back Breece Hall has not played since Week 3 due to a quad injury, but it appears he won't make his return to the lineup in Week 7 against the Miami Dolphins. Hall logged some practice time ahead of this AFC East rivalry matchup, and he's officially listed as questionable against Miami. However, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Hall is unlikely to suit up in this matchup. #Jets star RB Breece Hall, attempting to return from a quad strain after missing three games, is unlikely to play today, sources say. He may work out to see if he can go, but Hall hasn’t been a full participant yet. It's a bit early. Earlier in the week, Jets beat reporter Brian Costello expressed optimism about Hall's status, sharing that the star running back was moving well in practice despite being listed as a limited participant. Still, the fact that Hall was not able to practice in full makes it tough for him to return from a multi-week absence. So far this season, Hall has 51 carries for 163 yards and a score in 2026, adding 10 catches for 102 yards as a receiver. He's a dual-threat back that is one of the leading pieces for this Jets offense, so even getting him back in a limited capacity would give the team a massive boost. With Hall out, the Jets have turned to Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis as their top two options out of the backfield. Allen would handle the majority of the workload if Hall sits, and the two likely would split touches even if Hall is able to go. Currently, DraftKings Sportsbook only has touchdown scorer props for New York's running backs, listing Allen at -110, Hall at -110 and Davis at +650. Allen has seen goal-line looks at times this season since he's a bigger back, and he should see his odds jump once Hall is officially ruled out. Is Breece Hall Playing Today? away.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
away.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

away.headline: Miami Dolphins injury report: Rookie WR Caleb Douglas back for Jets
away.blurb: Douglas had been out since Week 2 when he suffered a sprained ankle against the San Francisco 49ers. Despite missing the last three games for 0-5 Miami, Douglas leads the Dolphins with 56.5 reception yards per game. Linebacker Willie Gay was ill and missed Thursday's practice. Hafley said he was feeling better on Friday morning and was limited at practice in the afternoon. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Promising rookie safety/linebacker Kyle Louis has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list since injuring his knee in the season-opener at Las Vegas. Hafley said he wants to wait until Friday's practice to determine if Louis will be activated. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. The Jets likely will be missing LB Kiko Mauigo (quad), OL Max Mitchel (concussion), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee) and EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), who all did not practice on Thursday. News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals MIAMI DOLPHINS Miami Dolphins injury report: Rookie WR Caleb Douglas back for Jets Nick Pugliese Palm Beach Post Updated Oct. 23, 2026, 4:30 p.m. ET The Miami Dolphins finally will have rookie receiver Caleb Douglas back on the field Sunday when they play at the New York Jets . "Caleb will play," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said at his Friday press conference. Meanwhile, quarterback Malik Willis, who did not throw during the bye week with an injured right thumb, has been practicing and is good to go. Hafley said running back Jaylen Wright (foot) will play. Tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) said Thursday that he's good to go. "He has stayed sharp but you're talking about a rookie who hasn't played much football," Hafley said. One new face Dolphins fans will see Sunday is placekicker Zane Gonzalez. Hafley talked about Gonzalez replacing Riley Patterson as the team's placekicker earlier in the week. He said it wasn't meant as a message. "We felt it was best for our team going forward," Hafley said. "Zane did a great job when he was here and then he was injured." The Bucs may or may not get Baker Mayfield back for this contest, but it will be a heated rivalry game regardless. It will also be crucial for the Buccaneers to cut into Carolina's division lead, so it could be a tough game regardless of how the two teams are perceived right now. What are the experts saying? Panthers vs. Buccaneers Week 7 NFL expert picks Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) plays against the Philadelphia Eagles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around." His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff is picking a Panthers win, 24-16, betting on the Bryce Young-led offense to continue clicking at home. SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte. "Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face... I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate," he wrote. Here's how the rest of the SI staff is predicting this one: Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers John Pluym: Panthers Matt Verderame: Panthers Peter Dewey: Panthers Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer disagrees, predicting a 24-17 win. "Jalon Daniels is doing his best to keep the Bucs' competitive with help from the running game. The defense is also bringing a good pass rush of late. Bryce Young is locked in passing all over the field for the Panthers, however and their running game is red-hot with Chuba Hubbard," he wrote. picks.headline: Will the Panthers beat the Buccaneers? Here are our staff predictions
picks.blurb: The Carolina Panthers will return home after a tough win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Awaiting them is their second divisional matchup, this time hosting the 1-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Baker Mayfield is on track to return, and based on his never-ending and pointless crusade against the Panthers, that is no surprise. Will he be able to turn the tables on the NFC South leaders, or will the Panthers continue their solid start to the season? Here's what the Panthers on SI staff thinks will happen this afternoon. Mark Livingston: Panthers 27, Buccaneers 20 I'm starting to trust this Panthers team, and I don't think I would've said that a few weeks ago. The defense has looked much better, Bryce Young finally has Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan together, and Carolina keeps finding ways to win. Tampa Bay will probably hang around because these NFC South games are rarely easy, but I think the Panthers are the better team right now. Give me Carolina at home. Russell Baxter: Panthers 28, Buccaneers 16 The Bucs let one get away last week after squandering a 16-3 fourth-quarter lead to the Steelers. The Panthers did exactly what they needed to in knocking off the short-handed Eagles. Bryce Young's 11 TD tosses have gone to six different players and should be able to have success against the league's 20th-ranked pass defense. It's a divisional game, and Dave Canales's club should hold serve at home via a comfortable victory. Zach Roberts: Panthers 24, Buccaneers 17 Maybe Baker Mayfield returns, maybe he doesn't. That doesn't make much of a material difference to me. He was playing horribly before he got hurt, and he's magically going to be good while nursing a throwing-hand injury? And potentially without Emeka Egbuka? I don't buy it. The Buccaneers won't be bringing much firepower against the improving Panthers' defense. On the other side, Tampa Bay's defense is quietly legitimate, but they haven't exactly faced a murderer's row of offenses in the first six weeks. They also blitz a lot (43.8%, third-most in NFL), and that doesn't really impact Bryce Young (NFL-best 0.36 EPA/dropback against the blitz). Not to mention, Tampa doesn't get home with the blitzes, as they have the second-worst pressure rate in the NFL. With Taylor Moton back, Carolina's offensive line is in better shape, so Tampa Bay's strength isn't going to translate. The rivalry nature will prevent a blowout, but Carolina should control this one. Preston Palm: Panthers 21, Buccaneers 17 This just feels like a slugfest type of game. Tampa Bay is coming in desperate, starting the season 1-5, and Baker Mayfield returns and is an ultra-competitor. The Buccaneers' defense is exceptional against the run, which could lead to an inefficient day for Bryce Young throwing the ball. Both teams will have moments, but Carolina’s offense has been too good not to make just a few more plays to edge out a division win. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.blurb: Mayfield, who has missed the last three games after dislocating his right thumb in Week 3, continues to make progress toward a potential return. The veteran quarterback was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday, providing optimism that he could be back under center when Tampa Bay travels to Carolina. Elsewhere on the injury report, running back Bucky Irving (illness) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (illness) were upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey (illness) also improved to full participation. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf), and linebacker Christian Rozeboom (finger) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. was also held out for rest. For Carolina, outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) remained out of practice Thursday. Running back Chuba Hubbard, linebacker Devin Lloyd, offensive tackle Taylor Moton, and tight end Darren Waller all returned as full participants after receiving rest Wednesday. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. Bettors are going to want to monitor Baltimore's practice report on Thursday, as it could solidify Jackson's status for Sunday's game. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. During the Bengals' matchup with the Ravens, Cincinnati will be seeking to extend its record to 4-2, which is what all three of the other AFC North teams currently remain tied at going into Week 7. However, due to the early bye week, the Bengals currently sit at 3-2, putting them last in the division. Before the injury news came down, the matchup had been widely anticipated as the toughest test yet for Cincinnati's newly revamped defensive line, with Jackson named as the league MVP for the 2019 and 2023 seasons. However, Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense are still expected to be in for quite a defensive challenge from the Ravens on Sunday: As the Bengals take to the field at M&T Bank Stadium, it will mark the first time that Burrow will face off against Trey Hendrickson on an opposing team's defensive line. This comes after the star edge rusher, who led the NFL in sacks in 2024, left Cincinnati last year for Baltimore following a prolonged contract dispute with the Bengals front office. home.headline: NFL experts were already picking the Bengals before the Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson
home.blurb: Bengals fans looking for outside belief after the bye had plenty of it before Saturday, and the injury news only added to it. Most national analysts picked Cincinnati at M&T Bank Stadium while Lamar Jackson was still questionable, and with Jackson ruled out, the line has flipped to Bengals by about 2.5 . That fits the tone of our bold predictions for Sunday . SI’s staff went 5-3 for Cincinnati , with Albert Breer and Conor Orr among the five. Jeff Zrebiec and Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic both took the Bengals. “I think the Ravens will have a hard time stopping a fresh and healthy Bengals team and Cincinnati will win,” Zrebiec wrote for The Athletic . Dehner liked the Bengals “especially if Jackson can’t go or is limited in his mobility.” Here’s the pushback. Bleacher Report’s staff went 4-3 for Baltimore against the spread when the Ravens were laying 2.5, and Brad Gagnon, who picked the Bengals to win the AFC North, is among the four. Gary Davenport wrote that “even if he sits, the Ravens are the pick here,” pointing to Zac Taylor’s 3-4 record off a bye. “The Ravens get after Joe Burrow, lean on Derrick Henry and win by a field goal,” he wrote for Bleacher Report . Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk took Baltimore 28-24, though his case began with “The Ravens need Lamar Jackson to return.” The Ravens’ own team site counted 36 of 47 pundits picking the Bengals. Here’s how the major outlets see it. Six of seven CBS Sports experts took Cincinnati straight up, with Ryan Wilson the lone Ravens pick, on the CBS expert board . John Breech has the Bengals winning 27-24, siding with the healthier quarterback in his CBS Sports picks . Four of five NFL.com analysts picked Cincinnati: Jeremy Bergman (27-24), Gennaro Filice (25-20), Bobby Kownack (28-27) and Dan Parr (27-25). Brooke Cersosimo was the lone holdout at 28-25 Ravens. Filice leaned on the Lawrence trade . “This is exactly why the Bengals traded the No. 10 overall pick for Dexter Lawrence,” Filice wrote in NFL.com’s Week 7 picks , citing Cincinnati’s league-leading 23% stuff rate. He also warned that “even if it’s Tyler Huntley, Baltimore can still pound the rock with Derrick Henry.” ESPN’s panel went 2-1 for the Bengals. Pamela Maldonado has Cincinnati 27-24, Seth Walder has it 26-24 and Eric Moody took Baltimore 27-24. Before the Jackson news, ESPN’s Football Power Index gave the Bengals a 54% win probability, and Walder’s bold prediction has Lawrence recording a sack. Sports Illustrated and The Athletic Bleacher Report and Pro Football Talk That’s a lot of national support for a team Burrow says isn’t respected like it was . “We want to be 4-2 and controlling our own destiny, and it really starts this week,” Burrow told reporters this week . In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Broncos Predictions vs. Cardinals: Bo Nix's Reckoning - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef 5 Bold Broncos Predictions vs. Cardinals: Bo Nix's Reckoning DENVER, CO - AUGUST 16: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix 10 looks on. | Dustin Bradford / IMAGO / Icon Sportswire Erick Trickel Sun, October 25, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Denver Broncos are preparing to take on the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The Cardinals are a feisty 2-4 team and are already exceeding expectations. This isn't a gimme game, despite what some people say. That being said, the Cardinals aren't exactly a good team either. The Broncos can't overlook this opponent, but this game is a chance to do some maintenance on offense and get the unit firing on all cylinders. And now it's time for this week's bold predictions. If the Broncos can realize these predictions, it could put them on the winning track for the rest of the season. Bo Nix Has Six Explosive Pass Plays (20-Plus Yards) Bo Nix warms up pre-game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nix has been seeing ghosts when looking deep after some early interceptions and near turnovers, which explains, in part, the ultra-conservative passing approach we've seen for weeks. This is a good game to work on correcting his hesitancy, as the Cardinals rank 31st in explosive pass-play rate allowed. The Cardinals suffer multiple coverage breaks per game. They have serious issues with their linebacker coverage, and their secondary isn't the best. The Broncos have no better opponent remaining on the schedule than Arizona to help Nix break out of his shell. The Nix reckoning is coming. RJ Harvey Finishes With 150-Plus Scrimmage Yards RJ Harvey makes a play. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This pairs with my previous prediction; there is ample opportunity to get Harvey involved in the passing and running game. The Cardinals are the NFL's fourth-worst defense when it comes to covering running backs, despite having one of the lowest rates of targets to backs. Part of this is due to Arizona's secondary issues. The Cardinals' linebackers will be mismatched covering Harvey, and they struggle against outside runs, which is where the Broncos' second-year back can be used in the ground game. Harvey finishes with 100-plus receiving and 50-plus rushing yards. Jacoby Brissett Sacked Six Times Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper celebrate a big play. | Dustin Bradford / IMAGO / Icon Sportswire The Cardinals haven't allowed many sacks this year (only 12), and they have the eighth-lowest sack percentage and pressure rate. However, they do allow one of the fastest times to pressure (sixth-fastest). Given how much pressure the Broncos can generate, as long as they can bring down Brissett, they're poised to have a big day in the sack department.If this prediction comes true, it'll be only the third time in franchise history that the Broncos will have posted three straight games with at least five sacks. This pass rush is on a roll, and that momentum continues in the desert. Jahdae Barron Gets a Pick-Six Jahdae Barron celebrates a big play. | Dustin Bradford / IMAGO / Icon Sportswire Thanks to the pressure up front and forcing a mistake from Brissett, Barron nabs an interception and returns it to the house. Barron is aggressive in coverage, and it sometimes backfires, but it pays off in this game. Brissett throws an underneath route under pressure, and Barron jumps it for the first pick-six of his career. He actually had one as a rookie, but it was called back due to a defensive holding penalty far away from the play. Broncos Get a Return Touchdown Marvin Mims Jr. returns a punt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Through the first six games, the Broncos have gotten close to a return touchdown. Harvey in particular has had multiple long returns that were a block or an avoided tackle away from being a touchdown. The Cardinals have lapses on kickoff coverage, which create the opening for a special teams touchdown.The Broncos have had a third-phase score brewing for weeks, but the stars finally align against Arizona, whether it's Harvey or Marvin Mims Jr. Today's best reads Bo Nix Breakout? away.blurb: Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was limited in practice this week with a chest injury before logging a full session on Friday. Waddle briefly left Denver's Week 6 win on Thursday night against the Seattle Seahawks, but he returned to the game in the second half. The Broncos star had four catches in the win, though the entire Denver passing offense has struggled this season. Bo Nix has not gotten going under center, and it's led to a rather pedestrian stat line for Waddle. He has 38 targets on the season, yet he's turned them into just 22 catches for 228 yards and a score. Waddle also has two carries for 23 yards. Outside of a big Week 2 against Jacksonville (eight catches 138 yards), Waddle has 35 or fewer receiving yards in every other game. Denver traded a first-round pick to Miami for Waddle in the offseason, so at some point the team needs to get him going with Nix at quarterback. This week, the SI Betting team has a player prop for both Nix and Waddle in Sunday's matchup with the two-win Cards. That could lead to big things for Waddle, who is due for another touchdown after having scored just one through his first six games as a Bronco. He's a great bet to score on Sunday at 2-1 odds. away.blurb: Given the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos faced to get to 4-2, they earned those three days. The question is whether that chance to breathe gave Sean Payton enough time to tweak the Broncos' offense, dig Bo Nix out of his slump, and get the run game firing on all cylinders. The Broncos are starting to get healthier. That may be a relative term, given that three players have been ruled out, but it's more about the caliber of players returning. Surtain is questionable after returning to practice on Wednesday . He was limited all three days this week, so if he's fully healthy, he'll play. If not, the Broncos will be wise and wait until Week 8 to insert him back into the lineup. Coleman is also listed as questionable, but only because Sean Payton wants Arizona to wonder for as long as possible whether the Broncos will actually activate their rookie running back. The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from injured reserve earlier this week. It's great to see Moss back to full participation. And Waddle has been fully cleared, though he was limited the first two days of the week. Badie, Elliss, and Hufanga are out this week. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Badie and Elliss placed on IR to make room for Coleman and the return of veteran rush linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who's expected to come back from the commissioner's exempt list this week. NFL.com Experts Rolling With Broncos In Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Brewers' stunning comeback NFL.com Experts Rolling With Broncos In Week 7 (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Matt Wadleigh Sun, October 25, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Denver Broncos survived a Thursday Night Football showdown against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 with a 17-14 win. It wasn't pretty, and the offense is still trying to find its identity, even with Sean Payton taking over the play-calling duties. In Week 7, the Broncos enter with a 4-2 record, and they will face the 2-4 Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. Arizona lost four in a row before Mike LaFleur led his team to an 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams, which just so happen t be LaFleur's former employer. The Cardinals have plenty of injuries, so everything bodes well for the Broncos going into Week 7. Here were all five of the score predictions: Cersosimo: Cardinals win, 24-23 Parr said the Cardinals win over the Rams was partly because of a "unquestionably benefited" gameplan, especially since LaFleur has a lot of familiarity with the Rams since he was in LA before being hired by Arizona. Parr also said this could be a perfect "get right" game for Broncos QB Bo Nix, and he certainly needs it after he has gotten off to a sluggish start this season. Of course, having Davis Webb call plays and then switching back to Sean Payton hasn't helped Nix much, and the offense still looked off despite defeating the Super Bowl champions. Of Arizona's four losses this season, three of them have come by double digits, and two of them by 20 or more points, so it's been a mixed bag of results for the Cardinals. Entering Week 7, the Broncos are 4-2 and in the playoff race, but that still might not be enough for them to be in the contenders conversation, even with a win, as was discussed in a recent podcast episode on the Roundtable Sports site. Now, a Broncos loss to the Cardinals might raise plenty of red flags in Denver, especially with the games after that coming against the Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers before a Week 10 bye. Let's see if the NFL.com experts get the pick right.

Waddle briefly left Denver's Week 6 win on Thursday night against the Seattle Seahawks, but he returned to the game in the second half. The Broncos star had four catches in the win, though the entire Denver passing offense has struggled this season. Bo Nix has not gotten going under center, and it's led to a rather pedestrian stat line for Waddle. He has 38 targets on the season, yet he's turned them into just 22 catches for 228 yards and a score. Waddle also has two carries for 23 yards. Outside of a big Week 2 against Jacksonville (eight catches 138 yards), Waddle has 35 or fewer receiving yards in every other game. Denver traded a first-round pick to Miami for Waddle in the offseason, so at some point the team needs to get him going with Nix at quarterback. This week, the SI Betting team has a player prop for both Nix and Waddle in Sunday's matchup with the two-win Cards. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.headline: Rams-Raiders injury report: Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman miss practice
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman both missed practice. Landman is in the concussion protocol, while McDuffie is still recovering from a groin injury that caused him to sit out Week 6 against the Cardinals. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. After dropping their last two games, the Los Angeles Rams are back to work in advance of their Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . The injury bug bit the Rams hard on Sunday, as Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford and Blake Grupe were all lost to IR, so Los Angeles will be shorthanded against Vegas this week. They won't make any excuses, though. Sean McVay said the Rams are monitoring McDuffie's progress to see if he'll be ready to go against the Raiders. McDuffie and Landman were the only players who did not participate in practice. Josh Wallace has a calf injury but was a full participant, as was Colby Parkinson (shoulder). away.headline: NFL Week 7 Injury Report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua Listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN’s Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders’ official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "The Chiefs, who’ve never fielded a top-15 rushing attack during Mahomes’ time as a starter, rank second with an average of 159.8 ground yards per game," Kownack wrote. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. Chiefs at Seahawks SNF: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction This is technically the second meeting between these two teams this year, following an ugly preseason tie in August that featured mostly second and third-string players. Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid watches play against the Seattle Seahawks during the game at Arrowhead Stadium. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 52.8%, Seahawks 46.8%. While Seattle boasts one of the best home-field advantages in the sport, the matchup predictor still gives the undefeated Chiefs a slight edge to maintain their perfect record. Chiefs on SI's Take Usually, the matchup predictor closely mirrors what traditional betting lines are forecasting. However, that isn't the case for this contest. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win.
